title: Is Apple Stock a Buy After Earnings? | AAPL Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc asks why Apple fell over 3% after a strong quarter, and whether the dip is a buying opportunity. Net sales rose to $114.5 billion for the quarter ended 26 September 2026, with product sales outgrowing services — surprising ahead of the holiday quarter and the new iPhone Duo launch, as many buyers bought ahead of the release. iPhone sales jumped to $57.6 billion from $49 billion a year earlier, and to $254 billion for the full year from $209 billion; China sales rose to $17.5 billion from $14.5 billion, and nine-month China sales to $82.4 billion from $64 billion, while Nike, Starbucks and Tesla struggled there. Operating income rose about 10% to roughly $35.66 billion despite soaring memory and storage costs, which have risen triple digits since the AI boom. Apple generated $145 billion of operating cash flow over twelve months against barely $9 billion of capex, and spent $86 billion buying back stock, keeping an asset-light model (net plant and equipment just $52 billion, versus almost $80 billion of quarterly spend at Amazon). Yet the shares were already up over 20% in 2026 at a forward PE above 34, and his DCF value is $204 against $338 going into results. Call: AAPL — HOLD (reiterated from 12 October) — excellent performance, still overvalued, wait for a better entry. Auto-captions garble the sponsor name and one operating-income figure.
